samples.guide: Use familiar concrete words, explicit subjects, one idea per clause and clear repetition. Use correct case, aspect and agreement. Cyrillic only, without Latin transliteration or added stress marks.
samples.brief: Two friends at a railway station discover their tickets are for different destinations.

content.title: Два билета
content.story:
Анна и Иван стоят на вокзале. У Анны в руке билет. У Ивана тоже есть билет.

— Наш поезд скоро, — говорит Анна. — Где твой билет?

— Вот. У меня есть билет в Москву, — говорит Иван.

Анна смотрит на Ивана.

— В Москву? У меня есть билет в Тулу. Мы едем в Тулу!

Иван смотрит на свой билет. На билете написано: «Москва».

Анна показывает свой билет. На её билете написано: «Тула».

— У нас билеты в разные города, — говорит Иван.

Рядом стоит скамейка. Анна и Иван садятся на скамейку. Иван держит два билета и ещё раз смотрит на них.

— Да, мой билет в Москву, а твой — в Тулу. Что теперь делать?

Анна смотрит на кассу.

— Давай спросим там.

content.title: Разные билеты
content.story:
Анна и Иван на вокзале. У Анны маленькая сумка. У Ивана большой рюкзак. Друзья стоят рядом и ждут поезд.

Анна достаёт билет.

— У меня есть билет. Я еду в Москву, — говорит Анна.

Иван тоже достаёт билет.

— У меня есть билет. Я еду в Казань, — говорит Иван.

Анна смотрит на Ивана.

— В Казань? Но мы едем вместе!

— Да, вместе, в Москву, — говорит Иван.

Иван смотрит на свой билет ещё раз. На билете слово «Казань».

Анна показывает свой билет. На её билете слово «Москва».

— У нас разные билеты, — говорит Анна. — Я еду в Москву, а ты едешь в Казань.

— Да. Это разные города, — говорит Иван.

Рядом стоит поезд. Иван смотрит на поезд, потом на Анну.

— Анна, что мы теперь делаем?

glossary.meaning: And; joins people or actions.
Railway station. «вокзале» is prepositional singular after «на», meaning at the station.
At or on with the prepositional case: at the station or on the ticket.
With a person's name or pronoun in the genitive, expresses possession: someone has something.
Small. «маленькая» is feminine singular to agree with «сумка».
Bag; feminine noun.
Big or large; masculine singular here, agreeing with «рюкзак».
Backpack; masculine noun.
Friend. «Друзья» is the irregular plural: friends.
To stand or be standing. «стоят» is plural; «стоит» is singular, describing the stationary train.
Nearby or next to each other.
To wait for. «ждут» means they are waiting for the train.
Train. The same written form is used as the subject and as the object of waiting or looking.
To take out. «достаёт» means takes out, here a ticket; present singular.
Ticket. «билет» is singular; «билете» means on the ticket after «на»; «билеты» is plural.
I have. Literally a possession construction with «у» plus genitive «меня» and «есть».
I; the subject form of the first-person singular pronoun.
To travel or go by transport. «еду» means I am going, «едем» we are going, and «едешь» you are going.
To, before a destination in the accusative case; used here for travel to a city.
To say or speak. «говорит» means says; present singular.
Also or too; Ivan takes out a ticket as Anna does.
To look at someone or something; «на» takes the accusative in this construction.
But; introduces a contrast or unexpected problem.
We; the subject pronoun for the two friends together.
Together; travelling with each other.
Yes; confirms what has been said.
One's own. «свой билет» refers to the ticket belonging to the person doing the action.
Once more or again; Ivan checks his ticket again.
Word; here the city name printed on a ticket.
To show. «показывает» means shows; present singular.
Her, indicating possession: her ticket. This possessive form does not change with the noun's case.
We have; «нас» is the genitive form of the pronoun meaning we after «у».
Different; not the same. «разные» is plural, describing the tickets and cities.
Whereas or but; contrasts Anna's destination with Ivan's.
You; singular, informal subject pronoun used between friends.
These are, in «Это разные города». Russian uses no present-tense word for are here.
City. «города» is nominative plural here: cities.
Then or next; marks the next action.
What; asks what action the friends are taking.
Now; at this point, after discovering the problem.
To do. «делаем» means we do or we are doing; in the final question, asks what they do now.

materialIssues: «На билете написано» introduces an impersonal passive construction beyond the simplest explicit-subject clauses; its contextual definition helps, but its structure remains unexplained.
«Что теперь делать?» and «Давай спросим там» introduce an infinitive question and a first-person-plural perfective suggestion. Both are natural, but add grammatical load for an introductory reader.
«Иван держит два билета» assumes an unmentioned transfer of Anna's ticket. This is a minor continuity gap rather than a contradiction.
«садятся», «держит» and «на них» receive no support despite introducing useful action vocabulary and a pronoun reference requiring case interpretation.
strengths: Clear destination contrast, repeated ticket checks and mostly short, concrete clauses.
All supplied glossary meanings and listed forms fit their contexts.
The ticket-office suggestion creates a natural unresolved next step.

materialIssues: «Я еду в Казань» followed by «Да, вместе, в Москву» makes Ivan appear to acknowledge two incompatible destinations before checking again. Confusion is plausible, but an explicit correction or surprised reaction would clarify the intended discovery.

«что мы теперь делаем?» is grammatical, but the present-tense question is less idiomatic for seeking the next course of action than «Что нам теперь делать?». This is a contextual phrasing preference, not a grammatical error.

«свой билет», «На её билете» and «У нас» introduce reflexive possession, invariant possessive «её» and a genitive pronoun construction. These add load beyond simple subject–verb clauses, although the notes explain them accurately.
strengths: Broad contextual support covers common words, inflected forms, motion verbs and case-dependent constructions rather than merely listing translations.
All supplied notes are contextually accurate; the explanations distinguish «на» with location from «смотреть на» with the accusative.
Concrete actions and repeated destination names aid comprehension.
The final question leaves an appropriate unresolved practical problem.
